prompt.brief: Design an end-to-end ML platform that trains models, validates artifacts, deploys them safely, supports A/B experiments, and monitors quality and latency in production.
successSignals: Version datasets, code, features, model artifacts, evaluation results, and deployment policy as one reproducible lineage.
Separate expensive training from a low-latency inference fleet and use canaries or A/B routing for controlled rollout.
Gate promotion on offline metrics, fairness and safety checks, resource limits, and reproducible signatures.
Detect drift, rollback quickly, protect model and feature data, and make every run resumable and auditable.

functional: Register datasets and experiments, launch training, evaluate candidate models, and store immutable artifacts.
Deploy a selected model to shadow, canary, A/B, and full-production stages with traffic and rollback controls.
Collect inference metrics, feedback, drift signals, lineage, cost, and approval evidence for each deployment.
nonFunctional: Target p95 inference latency below 100 ms with warm replicas and bounded feature and model lookups.
Scale training jobs and experiment telemetry independently from online inference traffic.
Never deploy an unverified artifact; make training, evaluation, rollout, and metric ingestion idempotent.
Keep the last healthy model available during registry, feature-store, or new-model failure.
scaleAssumptions: Run hundreds of experiments weekly, train on terabyte-scale datasets, and serve 100K inference requests per second.
Partition experiment metadata by project and telemetry by model version and time; isolate high-volume producers.
Retain immutable artifacts and sampled inference events while keeping online features and model replicas bounded.

deepDives.title: Partitioning and hot keys
points: Partition End-to-end ML platform by its primary read and write keys, then isolate hot tenants, users, items, or regions.
Bound End-to-end ML platform work with backpressure and queue isolation so one hot key cannot dominate the cluster.

tradeoffs.title: Strong consistency versus throughput
tradeoffs.recommendation: Strongly protect the business commit and use versioned eventual projections for high-volume reads.
tradeoffs.caution: Making every derived read synchronous increases coordination and tail latency.

tradeoffs.title: Push versus pull processing
tradeoffs.recommendation: Push bounded events to workers and pull durable snapshots on reads or recovery.
tradeoffs.caution: Unbounded fanout or full scans make bursts and hot keys expensive.

tradeoffs.title: Managed service versus custom control
tradeoffs.recommendation: Start with managed primitives where their limits match the access pattern, then isolate replaceable interfaces.
tradeoffs.caution: Provider defaults do not remove the need for quotas, replay, observability, and data lifecycle design.

commonMistakes: Putting all work on the synchronous request path.
Choosing a data store before writing the access patterns and consistency contract.
Ignoring retries, duplicate events, late data, deletion, privacy, or authorization.
Leaving hot partitions, backpressure, stale reads, and recovery unspecified.
Allowing unbounded requests or exports to compete with normal traffic.

followUps.question: What happens when the primary worker is unavailable?
followUps.answer: Acknowledge only after the durable boundary, serve the last acceptable projection, queue retryable work, and replay or reconcile after recovery.

followUps.question: How would you support a tenfold traffic spike?
followUps.answer: Pre-scale partitions, apply admission control and backpressure, isolate hot keys, cache immutable snapshots, and make freshness degradation visible.

followUps.question: How do you verify correctness?
followUps.answer: Use idempotency metrics, version gaps, sampled source-to-projection comparisons, replay tests, and a shadow rebuild before repair.

rubric.description: The answer defines training, evaluation, deployment, rollback, scale, latency, durability, and failure contracts.
Entities and model/version keys support training, validation, rollout, monitoring, privacy, and lifecycle changes.
Partitioning, cache behavior, queues, backpressure, and hot-key handling are explicit.
Idempotency, replay, recovery, degraded reads, and observability protect committed state.
The candidate can explain End-to-end ML platform consistency, push/pull, managed services, and the scale boundary.
